edits.content:
## Compare Claims Precisely
- **Normalize the quantifiers and dependencies.** Identify what is fixed and what may vary; distinguish a single object from a family indexed by a parameter, and read “for every,” “there exists,” and “almost every” with their stated domains and measures. Check whether conditional hypotheses apply to the same object or parameter named in the conclusion.
- **Order options by implication, but validate each claim first.** A claim with extra detail is stronger only if it is true and its added conditions follow from the hypotheses. Compare what each option actually guarantees; do not select an option merely because it sounds more precise or ambitious.
- **Check strictness and quantitative bounds at edge cases.** Test universal strict inequalities and positive-gap claims against possible equality cases. Separate lower bounds from upper bounds, and do not infer a two-sided estimate from a one-sided existence result.
- **Use definitions to test added constraints.** Ask whether an extra geometric, structural, or algorithmic condition is compatible with the object being asserted. Keep existence, equivalence, decidability, and production of explicit witnesses distinct; assert only the level of conclusion supported.
